Super possible stupid question: how did you get everything so perfectly straight? I can never do it, even with a ruler and things like that o.O Also do you use a pencil first or just do everything with the micron? Lastly, can you give me Satan's number so that I, too, can sell my soul for this?

Not a stupid question! Firstly I'd say that the drawings are not as perfect as you might think, I do allow room for error to keep things fun and finish work at a reasonable speed. I also believe that some small "flaws" are what adds character and humanity to the work, so I don't aim for 100% accuracy. I draw them in pencil first, and use various drawing tools for this (see below). This pencil drawing is used as a tracing for the final ink version, which is done freehand without any tools/guides etc. Heres what the pencil drawing looks like, should help you understand how I get to the final product: http://i.imgur.com/NW90Wal.jpg http://i.imgur.com/r2mvYHv.jpg http://i.imgur.com/aQedZ8l.jpg http://i.imgur.com/z3f479d.jpg http://i.imgur.com/soHVhjz.jpg

Some of the guidelines have already been erased, but earlier on you would have seen a lot of straight lines and circles everywhere. You'll see theres a lot of underlying circles and stuff that are not visible in the final piece, rather used as guides for other things. Its basically all geometry for the first few hours, as I decide the size & position of all the elements and rule everything out. The first step is ruling a straight line up the EXACT center of the page. This one has to be really precise, because everything else will flow from the center line.

You'll need more than just a ruler. Some kind of squaring tool is essential, like this: http://i.imgur.com/SoHDLBa.jpg

Take the above tool, line it up to the center line you already drew on the page, and you can draw perfect horizontal/diagonal lines very easily and quickly. Once you have a horizontal line and a vertical line, you can use the center point to start measuring stuff out in the drawing. Lets say I want the face of the character to be 14cm wide. I just draw a horizontal line and then measure 7cm on each side of the center. Make a small mark at 7cm on both sides, and that gives me the 14cm width, perfectly centered on the page.

I use a lot of circles, so have a collection of circle templates: http://i.imgur.com/rcQLgxP.jpg

Compass is also needed, and was used a lot in the eagle design. It has a lot of circles that all originate around one central point in the middle of the beak, all done with compass. Get one that can hold a mechanical pencil if you want accuracy, its important to have clean and consistent lines. http://i.imgur.com/SuQD2K7.jpg

Heres another handy tool, the bendy ruler. It holds its shape, so can be used to duplicate a curve, or flip the ruler over to get a mirror image of the same curve: http://i.imgur.com/Dgs1GpM.jpg

There are also curve templates but I personally don't seem to use them often: http://i.imgur.com/UIxM9Ma.jpg

Regarding selling your soul: Shouldn't be necessary, I would suggest 'The War of Art' by Steven Pressfield, its an amazing motivator that has helped me a lot since discovering it.

If you're interested, I posted more advice here: https://voat.co/v/progress/comments/280775
